questions.background: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) holds an annual leaders’ summit, which also provides opportunities for bilateral diplomatic meetings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Kremlin statements or reliable news reporting quoting a Kremlin official, published by August 31, 2026. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the leader publicly identified as scheduled to meet Vladimir Putin bilaterally on the sidelines of the 2026 SCO summit to discuss the Ukraine war. The announced meeting schedule determines the answer; the meeting need not have taken place. Accepted Answer Format : The leader’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Kyrgyzstan holds the 2025–2026 SCO chairmanship for the late-August/September 2026 Bishkek summit. At the 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, the Kremlin explicitly announced Putin's bilateral meeting with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan as focused on the Ukraine conflict, while Putin also discussed Ukraine in bilaterals with Indian PM Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Given Turkey's active mediation posture and cultural ties to host Kyrgyzstan, Erdogan leads (35%), followed by guaranteed SCO full-member leaders Modi (24%) and Xi (20%, following their May 2026 Beijing summit), with smaller probabilities on Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko (amid June 2026 Ukraine-Belarus border tensions) and Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev.

local_articles.snippet: Organisers of the Sydney Marathon have taken a major branding error in their stride after an engraving mistake on the race medals inadvertently became a trending topic on social media. local_articles.snippet: In a week’s time, the proud runners finishing the Sydney Marathon in Australia will receive a medal showing the landmarks they have just sped past – plus one they definitely didn’t. (2) Crucially, the conference also passed formal authorization allowing Abbas and the executive committee to add outside independent candidates to the slate, clearing the key institutional hurdle; Abbas stated Saturday he hopes to reach an agreement with Segalovitz 'in the coming days,' and Haaretz cites a party source noting Segalovitz's addition 'could reshuffle the list selected by party members earlier in the day,' potentially into the No. 2 slot. Raising Yoav Segalovitz 0.48 -> 0.55 (strictly capped at 0.55 while talks remain unsigned and reshuffling Taha down from #2 faces internal sensitivity) and surging primary winner Walid Taha 0.17 -> 0.40 (wins if Segalovitz talks fail, slip past Sept 5, or place Segalovitz at #3/#4), while collapsing Alhwashla (0.015), Khatib-Yassin (0.01), and Hujirat (0.005); sum = 0.98 (0.02 residual for an alternative outside recruit).

local_articles.title: Hamilton says Ferrari strategy cost him a podium
local_articles.snippet: ZANDVOORT, Netherlands, Aug 23 - Lewis Hamilton said he could have been on the podium at Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix had Ferrari acted quicker to get him ahead of teammate Charles Leclerc. The seven-times Formula One world champion ended up a close fourth, losing ground in the championship battle, with Leclerc fifth. McLaren's Lando Norris won, with Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and George Russell second and third after they had switched places. Hamilton is now level on points with Russell and 59 behind Antonelli. Hamilton had told Ferrari he was quicker than Leclerc on a different tyre strategy but the team delayed doing anything for a lap before pitting Leclerc. "Let’s not hold ourselves up from a potentially better result,” Hamilton said over the radio.
